articles.title: Can the UK escape the public debt trap?
articles.snippet: Can the UK escape the public debt trap? Expert comment jon.wallace 10 September 2026 The UK’s mix of high fiscal deficits, rising bond yields, anaemic growth, high taxes and an impatient electorate can only be solved with politically brave choices. All major advanced economies have seen rising long-term bond yields over the past year. But with the ten-year gilt yield at 5.2 per cent on 9 Sept 2026, the UK’s long-term rates are the highest in the G7. US ten-year yields are 4.8 per cent, Germany’s are 3.4 per cent and Japan’s 2.9 per cent. Reasons for the UK’s relative weakness The UK’s relatively high long-term interest rate reflects in part its lack of other economies’ advantages.
